lessons.title: Find a problem through discovery
lessons.text:
An offer connects a narrow customer problem to a checked deliverable and a price hypothesis. AI does not create demand. Learn through real permission-based discovery where possible, but label rehearsals and never fabricate sales, experience or testimonials.

Ask three consenting potential users about their current workaround; keep simulations explicitly labelled. Inspect the supplied input before using any tool. Write the decision rules in your own words and calculate one small result independently. The reference output is an answer key for this deliberately bounded fixture, not proof of general capability.

Policy for this project: Include selling, delivery, checking and support time. Payment-country eligibility must be verified before selling; no false residency, borrowed accounts or bypassing provider restrictions. Learning completion does not require earning money.

For learners across regions underserved or excluded by mainstream providers: verify country eligibility, language, account/identity requirements, data terms, cost, quota and connectivity before choosing a cloud service. Use only legitimate available alternatives; never bypass restrictions or invent a country/account. No service access? Complete the labelled manual/fixture route without claiming a live AI run.

Project clinic: Discovery is listening before proposing automation. Ask about the most recent time the task occurred: what triggered it, who did it, how long it took, what went wrong and what the consequence was. Avoid leading questions such as 'Would you pay for my AI tool?' Ask permission to keep anonymous notes; do not record private documents or collect payment details. Three conversations reveal hypotheses, not a representative market.
lessons.example:
CONSTRUCTED DISCOVERY NOTE — NOT A REAL CUSTOMER
Role: owner of a fictional repair shop.
Recent task: copied five enquiry messages into a weekly job list.
Current workaround: paper notebook; owner checks every entry.
Problem hypothesis: duplicate transcription and missing appointment dates.
Unproven: willingness to pay, available budget, accessible payout route.
NEXT QUESTION: 'Can you describe the last time a missing date caused a problem?'

lessons.title: Build and break one sample
lessons.text:
An offer connects a narrow customer problem to a checked deliverable and a price hypothesis. AI does not create demand. Learn through real permission-based discovery where possible, but label rehearsals and never fabricate sales, experience or testimonials.

Choose checked reports, approved replies, verified content or a tiny web tool. Establish a baseline before changing prompts or code. Keep the original input immutable. Record expected values, observed values and whether each comparison passed. If the expected file conflicts with a justified policy, investigate rather than forcing a convenient match.

Policy for this project: Include selling, delivery, checking and support time. Payment-country eligibility must be verified before selling; no false residency, borrowed accounts or bypassing provider restrictions. Learning completion does not require earning money.

Project clinic: Choose one lane, not a general AI agency: a checked report, approved reply pack, verified content pack or tiny web calculator. Write acceptance criteria before building. A report buyer might require totals that reconcile, visible rejected rows and a readable one-page explanation. Make the same sample manually first so speed and accuracy can be compared. A synthetic shop example remains a portfolio demonstration until a real buyer supplies authorised requirements.
lessons.example:
SAMPLE OFFER LANE — CHECKED WEEKLY REPORT
Input: a fictional three-row expense table; no private customer records.
Deliverables: unchanged source.csv, checked summary.csv, a one-page report and rejection log.
Acceptance: category subtotals equal the grand total; unsupported causes are omitted.
CHANGE TEST: add one valid row; the total and narrative must both update.
NOT CLAIMED: a real customer, saved labour or earned revenue.

lessons.title: Price the full workflow
lessons.text:
An offer connects a narrow customer problem to a checked deliverable and a price hypothesis. AI does not create demand. Learn through real permission-based discovery where possible, but label rehearsals and never fabricate sales, experience or testimonials.

Include selling and support time, fees, rework and refund assumptions. Build one inspectable transformation or bounded AI prompt. Keep calculation and validation deterministic where possible. If you make a permitted hosted call, save the actual response separately from the authored examples and verify its material claims; the supplied reference never simulates a live model.

Policy for this project: Include selling, delivery, checking and support time. Payment-country eligibility must be verified before selling; no false residency, borrowed accounts or bypassing provider restrictions. Learning completion does not require earning money.

Project clinic: Pricing is a hypothesis, not a number copied from an income guide. In the fixture, a price of 30 minus tool cost 3 and fees 2 leaves 25 before tax. Four hours include two delivering, one selling and one supporting, so the effective return is 6.25 per hour before tax. Equipment, connectivity, foreign-exchange charges and additional rework may reduce it further. A refund of 10 leaves 15 and changes the return to 3.75. If no one pays, earned income is zero.
lessons.example:
HYPOTHETICAL ECONOMICS — GENERIC CURRENCY UNITS
Price: 30; tools: 3; transaction fees: 2.
Net before tax: 30 - 3 - 2 = 25.
Time: delivery 2h + selling 1h + support 1h = 4h.
Effective hourly return before tax: 25 / 4 = 6.25.
Refund scenario: (25 - 10) / 4 = 3.75.
These are assumptions to test, not a quoted market price or earnings result.

lessons.title: Check access and test the offer
lessons.text:
An offer connects a narrow customer problem to a checked deliverable and a price hypothesis. AI does not create demand. Learn through real permission-based discovery where possible, but label rehearsals and never fabricate sales, experience or testimonials.

Verify regional payout and identity rules, then use a small appropriate personalised approach with opt-outs. Change one assumption at a time and predict the result first. Retain the failure, the revision and the rerun evidence. A failure is useful information: hiding a bad output or editing a test target after seeing the answer destroys the value of the experiment.

Policy for this project: Include selling, delivery, checking and support time. Payment-country eligibility must be verified before selling; no false residency, borrowed accounts or bypassing provider restrictions. Learning completion does not require earning money.

Project clinic: Check access before accepting money: seller-country eligibility, supported receiving method, identity and business requirements, currencies, fees, payout timing and refund handling. Record the official source and date, not a guessed green tick. A locally agreed lawful payment route may be more practical than an unavailable global marketplace, but it still needs verification. Outreach must be appropriate, truthful and small enough to personalise. Mention a demonstration as a demonstration; never claim past clients or savings you have not established.
lessons.example:
ORIGINAL OUTREACH EXAMPLE — USE ONLY WHEN TRUE
Hello [name], I noticed [specific publicly visible task relevant to their work]. I made a small demonstration of [bounded deliverable] using fictional data. I do not know whether it fits your process. Would you be open to a brief look and a question about how you handle this now? No problem if not; I will not add you to a sequence.
BEFORE A PAID OFFER: verify the legitimate receiving route and agree scope.
LOG: permission, response, objection and next step—not assumed conversion rates.

lessons.title: Deliver ethically and hand over
lessons.text:
An offer connects a narrow customer problem to a checked deliverable and a price hypothesis. AI does not create demand. Learn through real permission-based discovery where possible, but label rehearsals and never fabricate sales, experience or testimonials.

Define scope, approvals, rights, revisions, accounting boundaries and support. Review what the fixture cannot establish. Explain who owns the decision, where human approval is needed and which access or professional constraints remain. Do not describe a small educational success as production readiness, certification, legal compliance or a guarantee.

Policy for this project: Include selling, delivery, checking and support time. Payment-country eligibility must be verified before selling; no false residency, borrowed accounts or bypassing provider restrictions. Learning completion does not require earning money.

For learners across regions underserved or excluded by mainstream providers: verify country eligibility, language, account/identity requirements, data terms, cost, quota and connectivity before choosing a cloud service. Use only legitimate available alternatives; never bypass restrictions or invent a country/account. No service access? Complete the labelled manual/fixture route without claiming a live AI run.

Supporting practice — Ethical records and professional boundaries: Keep revenue, costs, unpaid time and refunds separate. Preserve consent, client approval and conflicts of interest. Do not describe an educational price sheet as accounting, audit or tax advice. Applicable obligations depend on jurisdiction; involve a qualified professional when required. Add a dated cost ledger, confidentiality rule, conflict disclosure and a professional-review boundary.

Project clinic: Delivery requires agreement on inputs, scope, acceptance, revisions, payment and maintenance. Ask permission before sending client data to any cloud service; a client saying 'use AI' is not a blanket data-processing agreement. Keep a private cost ledger and record refunds accurately. Use the offer template to exclude medical, legal, tax, investment, safety and employment decisions. Hand over an exportable result and explain which changes need fresh checking; do not lock a learner or buyer into an undisclosed subscription.
lessons.example:
SCOPE EXAMPLE — NOT A LEGAL CONTRACT
Included: one fictional CSV-to-summary demonstration, checked totals, README and one revision.
Excluded: bookkeeping, tax filing, live account access, autonomous messages and ongoing hosting.
Acceptance: source totals reconcile; rejected rows and limitations are visible.
Authority: buyer reviews before use; no external action without separate approval.
Support boundary: fix agreed defects for the stated period; new requirements are a new scope.
Use qualified local advice for actual contracts and obligations.

lessons.title: Decide from actual evidence
lessons.text:
An offer connects a narrow customer problem to a checked deliverable and a price hypothesis. AI does not create demand. Learn through real permission-based discovery where possible, but label rehearsals and never fabricate sales, experience or testimonials.

Record acceptance, refunds and net return if a paid pilot occurred; otherwise report the real market-test result without invention. Deliver a reproducible bundle rather than a screenshot alone. Include inputs, rules, output, failure tests, a short README and residual limitations. Ask another person to follow the instructions if possible; self-review and actual external review must be labelled separately.

Policy for this project: Include selling, delivery, checking and support time. Payment-country eligibility must be verified before selling; no false residency, borrowed accounts or bypassing provider restrictions. Learning completion does not require earning money.

Project clinic: Decide from evidence rather than the excitement of a launch. Track conversations, relevant interest, offers, paid orders, accepted deliveries, refunds, costs and time as separate stages. A friend praising a demo is not a paid customer. A paid pilot is stronger evidence than an intention to buy, but one sale does not establish typical income or repeatable demand. If no buyer agrees, document the obstacle and choose a smaller test, a different problem or a stop decision. Completion rewards honest work and learning, not earning at any cost.
lessons.example:
CONSTRUCTED DECISION RECORD — NOT ACTUAL RESULTS
Conversations: 3; offer discussions: 1; paid orders: 0.
What is supported: one person agreed to discuss the problem.
What is NOT supported: demand at the proposed price, a repeatable sales channel or any earned income.
Decision: revise the sample around the observed missing-date problem and retest once.
If a real paid pilot occurs: log acceptance, refunds, actual costs and time with permission; redact identifying details.
